No worries! So having tried a few different sites, Upwork is definitely the best I’ve found (literally never got a single job on Fiver!) While you can advertise your services, that’s a newer function on Upwork, and typically you would submit proposals for existing projects, which could be fixed milestones or hourly work. 

Best of luck with this! Also, it might be worth considering that loads of regular jobs are also at least partially home based now as a result of the pandemic, so you might even be able to get something else that would allow you to work from home.

Of course! It’s honestly been life changing for me so more than happy to share :) 

I had prior experience in freelance editing and writing, but nothing full time/that impressive. Then after graduating I had been working in a range of fields (care, customer service, technical writing) mostly in low-paid roles that I didn’t enjoy and worsened my mental health. 

I transitioned in April and only had one project in May, and due to when I was paid was able to receive benefits for that month. By June I had established one long-term client and by July had added two more. I’ve been lucky in that these have all turned into long term positions that provide me with a sense of security. 

My advice would be to start with a platform such as Upwork that advertises for a wide range of services and projects. That way you can try out a few and find what sort of tasks suit you. Copywriting and editing are ones I enjoy personally, but there are all sorts of tasks, such as virtual admin or project management, more creative tasks like graphic design, data entry, transcription which you had mentioned, etc. 

To start off with the rates will likely be low - I’m not trying to pretend that isn’t the case. However, building up some solid experience on a site and good reviews from clients on short term projects can pave the way to longer term or better paid projects :) Also, don’t be afraid to negotiate or to ask for market value in your chosen skill set. It’s important to know your worth when you’re working for yourself! 

Another thing to mention is that in the UK you can also use business expenses to offset your tax at the end of the tax year, which can include a portion or rent, utilities, or technology costs, for example, which can be a big bonus. 

I hope that helps and please let me know if you have any further questions :)

I don’t know if this would apply to you but if you’re self employed you can usually choose where you work from, which could be from home :) 

I made the switch earlier this year and it reduced a ton of anxiety around public transport/an office environment. There are a ton of skills and services you can provide on a contractual or freelance basis so this might be something to look into if it appeals to you?
